content.content:
# Design document — carwatch

> **STATUS: M2 SKELETON.** 3–5 pages when complete. The handout calls these "the most
> leveraged hours of the whole project" — every hour of arguing here saves five of
> rewriting later.
>
> **Before submitting, run the three-isolated-workers check:** a design-only reviewer,
> a parts-only buyer who never sees the design, and a builder who only follows
> instructions must each succeed from their own section alone.

## 1. Architecture
>
> A diagram in the spirit of the handout's Figure 1: processes, threads, kernel
> components, data flows, **and rates on every arrow**. The rates are not decoration —
> they are what makes the mechanism justifications checkable.

```text
  OBD2 port
        │                          Pi power: the box's one USB-C input from the owner's
  ┌──────────────┐                 charger + a seconds-scale supercapacitor; off at rest,
  │              │                 clean shutdown at key-off (D-024)
  │ Bluetooth    │  RFCOMM tty         ┌────────────────┐
  │ OBD2 adapter │◀ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ▶│      obdd      │  Mode 01 requests,
  │ (D-019)      │  /dev/obd           │  tty reader    │  [N] req/s, round-robin (D-012)
  └──────────────┘                     └───────┬────────┘
                                               │ SPSC ring in shm, [N] samples/s,
                                               │ sequence-accounted; one consumer (D-031)
                                               ▼
                                       ┌────────────────┐
                                       │    storaged    │  append-only log; BEGIN/COMMIT
                                       │    [mech D]    │  batches, one fsync each (D-025)
                                       └───────┬────────┘
                                               │ committed records only, read from
                                               │ the log, [N] records/s (D-031)
                                               ▼
                                       ┌────────────────┐
                                       │    analyzed    │  bins → baselines → residuals
                                       │                │  → trends → model → FSM
                                       └───────┬────────┘
                                               │ verdicts, UDS
                                               ▼
   ┌────────────────┐       UDS        ┌────────────────┐  GPIOs
   │ obdctl         │◀────────────────▶│   supervisor   │──────────▶ tri-color light (D-027)
   │ query CLI,     │                  │   [mech E]     │            pulse = alive;
   │ 5 verbs        │       ┌─────────▶│                │            steady = not running
   └────────────────┘       │   UDS    └────────────────┘
   ┌────────────────┐       │          spawns, heartbeats and restarts, with backoff,
   │ status page    │◀──────┘          every process in this figure
   │ verdicts+report│──▶ phone: the box's own Wi-Fi AP, no upstream (D-013, D-028)
   └────────────────┘
```

`obdctl` and the status page never read samples themselves: they ask the supervisor, which
asks the process that holds the answer (D-013). `analyzed` never reads the ring (D-031).

**TODO(M2):** fill every `[N]`. Replace with a real figure in `docs/figures/`.

## 2. Mechanism mapping
>
> For each chosen menu item: which component implements it, and a justification **from
> the user's requirements**. The defense will test the justification, not the choice.
> Model the form on the handout's example: "the vibration analysis is meaningless above
> 2 ms of sampling jitter, hence SCHED_FIFO."

The committed rationale is `docs/DECISIONS.md` §B.1 (D-017); expand each row here with
the measured numbers that justify it. B and F were considered and declined: no Pi-side
sensor is added, so nothing in the design needs them (D-029).

| Menu item | Component | Justification from requirements | How measured |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D | `src/store/` | | recovery after mid-write power cut, N trials |
| E | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` | | `kill -9` any child; detection/degradation/recovery in the log |

## 3. Failure-mode table
>
> For each component: how it can fail, how the failure is **detected**, what the system
> **does**, and what the **log will show**. The soak test grades this table's honesty —
> so write the modes you are afraid of, not the ones you have already handled.

| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OBD2 adapter | Bluetooth link drops mid-drive (out of range, adapter asleep, unplugged) | hangup on the tty: `read` returns 0 or `EIO`, `poll` reports `POLLHUP` | degrade, do not restart-storm; reopen `/dev/obd` with backoff until the link returns | |
| OBD2 adapter | hangs or returns garbage (`?`, `NO DATA`, `BUFFER FULL`) | per-request timeout; reply parse failure | `ATZ` reset, then back off | |
| ECU | stops answering a PID (sensor unplugged) | request timeout, per PID (D-012) | mark PID absent, keep the rest | |
| obdd | crash / `kill -9` | supervisor `waitpid` | restart with backoff | |
| ring | consumer stalls, producer would overwrite | sequence gap accounting | | |
| storaged | disk full | | | |

# carwatch — CS370 term project
# Systems core is C17 and must stay -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean (CLAUDE.md §2.4).

CC       ?= gcc

# tools/ needs tomllib, which is Python 3.11+. The department machines put 3.9
# on PATH as python3, where boardcheck dies with ModuleNotFoundError before it
# can report anything useful. Pick the first interpreter that can actually parse
# the board; fall back to python3 so the error, if any, still comes from tools/.
PY       ?= $(shell for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11; do \
              command -v $$p >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              $$p -c 'import tomllib' >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo $$p; exit 0; }; \
            done; echo python3)
CSTD      = -std=c17
WARN      = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wvla
OPT      ?= -O2 -g
CPPFLAGS += -Iinclude -D_GNU_SOURCE
CFLAGS   += $(CSTD) $(WARN) $(OPT)
LDLIBS   += -lm -lpthread

BUILD    = build
BIN      = $(BUILD)/bin

ALL_SRC    = $(wildcard src/*/*.c)
# Library objects: everything except the per-daemon entry points.
COMMON_SRC = $(filter-out %/main.c,$(ALL_SRC))
COMMON_OBJ = $(COMMON_SRC:%.c=$(BUILD)/%.o)

DAEMONS    = obdd storaged analyzed supervisor obdctl
DAEMON_BIN = $(addprefix $(BIN)/,$(DAEMONS))

TEST_SRC   = $(wildcard tests/test_*.c)
TEST_BIN   = $(TEST_SRC:tests/%.c=$(BIN)/%)

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck soakcheck replay deploy clean boundary boardcheck \
        hwcheck hwdocs hwclean

all: $(DAEMON_BIN)

$(BIN)/obdd:       $(BUILD)/src/obd/main.o        $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/storaged:   $(BUILD)/src/store/main.o      $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/analyzed:   $(BUILD)/src/analysis/main.o   $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/supervisor: $(BUILD)/src/supervisor/main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/obdctl:     $(BUILD)/src/interface/main.o  $(COMMON_OBJ)

$(DAEMON_BIN):
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(BUILD)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@

$(BIN)/test_%: tests/test_%.c $(COMMON_OBJ)
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

test: $(TEST_BIN) boundary boardcheck
	@fail=0; for t in $(TEST_BIN); do \
		printf '%-28s ' "$$(basename $$t)"; \
		if $$t; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL; fail=1; fi; done; \
	exit $$fail

# CLAUDE.md §2.1 — a grader must be able to confirm the boundary in sixty seconds.
# No network client anywhere in the product except src/interface/.
boundary:
	@if grep -rnE '\b(curl_|SSL_|getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|socket)\b' src \
	     --include='*.c' --include='*.h' | grep -v '^src/interface/'; then \
		echo "BOUNDARY VIOLATION: network symbol outside src/interface/"; exit 1; \
	else echo "boundary                     PASS"; fi

# docs/milestones.md is the board (D-020) - every task, question and decision
# in the project is a checkbox there. Validate it in the same gate as the C.
boardcheck:
	@$(PY) tools/test_board.py

asan:
	$(MAKE) clean
	$(MAKE) test OPT="-O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer"

memcheck: $(TEST_BIN)
	@for t in $(TEST_BIN); do valgrind --error-exitcode=1 --leak-check=full $$t || exit 1; done

soakcheck: all
	./soak/run_soak.sh --mini

replay: all
	@test -n "$(FIX)" || { echo "usage: make replay FIX=fixtures/<name>"; exit 1; }
	./tools/replay.py --fixture $(FIX) --label replay

deploy: all
	@test -n "$(PI)" || { echo "usage: make deploy PI=pi@<host>"; exit 1; }
	rsync -a --exclude build --exclude .git ./ $(PI):~/carwatch/
	ssh $(PI) 'cd ~/carwatch && make'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- hardware
# KiCad 10. On Windows kicad-cli.exe is under
# "C:/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/" and is NOT on PATH by default:
#   make hwcheck KICAD="/c/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/kicad-cli.exe"
KICAD ?= kicad-cli
SCH    = electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.kicad_sch

# ERC as a build failure — the hardware equivalent of -Werror (CLAUDE.md 7.12).
hwcheck:
	@command -v $(KICAD) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { \
		echo "kicad-cli not found. Set KICAD=/path/to/kicad-cli"; exit 1; }
	$(KICAD) sch erc --exit-code-violations --format json \
	         -o electricalDrawing/erc.json $(SCH)
	@echo "erc                          PASS"

# Regenerate everything derived from the schematic. Never hand-edit the outputs.
hwdocs:
	@mkdir -p docs/figures
	$(KICAD) sch export svg --exclude-drawing-sheet -o docs/figures/ $(SCH)
	$(KICAD) sch export bom \
	         --fields "Reference,Value,Footprint,MPN,Datasheet,Qty" \
	         --group-by Value -o docs/hardware/bom.csv $(SCH)
	$(KICAD) sch export netlist -o electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.net $(SCH)
	@echo "Regenerated: schematic SVG, bom.csv, netlist."
	@echo "Commit the SVG — PRs touching hw must show a picture."

hwclean:
	rm -f electricalDrawing/erc.json electricalDrawing/drc.json

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

-include $(shell find $(BUILD) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)

except the read-only status page and report server in `src/interface/`, which serves the
box's own Wi-Fi access point and has no upstream connection (D-013, D-028). `grep -r` for
any network symbol outside that directory returns nothing, and that check is in
`make test`.

## 9. Changelog (added at M5)
>
> What M2's version got wrong. This section is graded and an empty one is not credible.
# carwatch — CS370 term project
# Systems core is C17 and must stay -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean (CLAUDE.md §2.4).

CC       ?= gcc

# tools/ needs tomllib, which is Python 3.11+. The department machines put 3.9
# on PATH as python3, where boardcheck dies with ModuleNotFoundError before it
# can report anything useful. Pick the first interpreter that can actually parse
# the board; fall back to python3 so the error, if any, still comes from tools/.
PY       ?= $(shell for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11; do \
              command -v $$p >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              $$p -c 'import tomllib' >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo $$p; exit 0; }; \
            done; echo python3)
CSTD      = -std=c17
WARN      = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wvla
OPT      ?= -O2 -g
CPPFLAGS += -Iinclude -D_GNU_SOURCE
CFLAGS   += $(CSTD) $(WARN) $(OPT)
LDLIBS   += -lm -lpthread

BUILD    = build
BIN      = $(BUILD)/bin

ALL_SRC    = $(wildcard src/*/*.c)
# Library objects: everything except the per-daemon entry points.
COMMON_SRC = $(filter-out %/main.c,$(ALL_SRC))
COMMON_OBJ = $(COMMON_SRC:%.c=$(BUILD)/%.o)

DAEMONS    = obdd storaged analyzed supervisor obdctl
DAEMON_BIN = $(addprefix $(BIN)/,$(DAEMONS))

TEST_SRC   = $(wildcard tests/test_*.c)
TEST_BIN   = $(TEST_SRC:tests/%.c=$(BIN)/%)

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck soakcheck replay deploy clean boundary boardcheck \
        hwcheck hwdocs hwclean

all: $(DAEMON_BIN)

$(BIN)/obdd:       $(BUILD)/src/obd/main.o        $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/storaged:   $(BUILD)/src/store/main.o      $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/analyzed:   $(BUILD)/src/analysis/main.o   $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/supervisor: $(BUILD)/src/supervisor/main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/obdctl:     $(BUILD)/src/interface/main.o  $(COMMON_OBJ)

$(DAEMON_BIN):
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(BUILD)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@

$(BIN)/test_%: tests/test_%.c $(COMMON_OBJ)
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

test: $(TEST_BIN) boundary boardcheck
	@fail=0; for t in $(TEST_BIN); do \
		printf '%-28s ' "$$(basename $$t)"; \
		if $$t; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL; fail=1; fi; done; \
	exit $$fail

# CLAUDE.md §2.1 — a grader must be able to confirm the boundary in sixty seconds.
# No network client anywhere in the product except src/interface/.
boundary:
	@if grep -rnE '\b(curl_|SSL_|getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|socket)\b' src \
	     --include='*.c' --include='*.h' | grep -v '^src/interface/'; then \
		echo "BOUNDARY VIOLATION: network symbol outside src/interface/"; exit 1; \
	else echo "boundary                     PASS"; fi

# docs/milestones.md is the board (D-020) - every task, question and decision
# in the project is a checkbox there. Validate it in the same gate as the C.
boardcheck:
	@$(PY) tools/test_board.py

asan:
	$(MAKE) clean
	$(MAKE) test OPT="-O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer"

memcheck: $(TEST_BIN)
	@for t in $(TEST_BIN); do valgrind --error-exitcode=1 --leak-check=full $$t || exit 1; done

soakcheck: all
	./soak/run_soak.sh --mini

replay: all
	@test -n "$(FIX)" || { echo "usage: make replay FIX=fixtures/<name>"; exit 1; }
	./tools/replay.py --fixture $(FIX) --label replay

deploy: all
	@test -n "$(PI)" || { echo "usage: make deploy PI=pi@<host>"; exit 1; }
	rsync -a --exclude build --exclude .git ./ $(PI):~/carwatch/
	ssh $(PI) 'cd ~/carwatch && make'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- hardware
# KiCad 10. On Windows kicad-cli.exe is under
# "C:/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/" and is NOT on PATH by default:
#   make hwcheck KICAD="/c/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/kicad-cli.exe"
KICAD ?= kicad-cli
SCH    = electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.kicad_sch

# ERC as a build failure — the hardware equivalent of -Werror (CLAUDE.md 7.12).
hwcheck:
	@command -v $(KICAD) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { \
		echo "kicad-cli not found. Set KICAD=/path/to/kicad-cli"; exit 1; }
	$(KICAD) sch erc --exit-code-violations --format json \
	         -o electricalDrawing/erc.json $(SCH)
	@echo "erc                          PASS"

# Regenerate everything derived from the schematic. Never hand-edit the outputs.
hwdocs:
	@mkdir -p docs/figures
	$(KICAD) sch export svg --exclude-drawing-sheet -o docs/figures/ $(SCH)
	$(KICAD) sch export bom \
	         --fields "Reference,Value,Footprint,MPN,Datasheet,Qty" \
	         --group-by Value -o docs/hardware/bom.csv $(SCH)
	$(KICAD) sch export netlist -o electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.net $(SCH)
	@echo "Regenerated: schematic SVG, bom.csv, netlist."
	@echo "Commit the SVG — PRs touching hw must show a picture."

hwclean:
	rm -f electricalDrawing/erc.json electricalDrawing/drc.json

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

-include $(shell find $(BUILD) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)

## 8. The Design Document (M2)

**3–5 pages** and the most leveraged hours of the whole project. Because every hour of
arguing here saves five of rewriting later. Required contents:

- **Architecture.** A diagram in the spirit of Figure 1: processes, threads, kernel
  components, data flows, and **rates on every arrow**.
- **Mechanism mapping.** For each chosen menu item: which component implements it, and a
  justification from the user's requirements (*"the vibration analysis is meaningless above
  2 ms of sampling jitter, hence `SCHED_FIFO`"*).
- **Failure-mode table.** For each component: how it can fail, how the failure is detected,
  what the system does about it, and what the log will show. The soak test (Section 3.4)
  will grade this table's honesty.
- **Storage and data.** What is stored, at what rate, in what format, with what retention,
  and what happens to it when the power dies mid-write.
- **Constraints and substitutions.** What the ideal build would use, what you're actually
  using, and what the gap costs: sensors downgraded, data synthesized or replayed, claims
  narrowed (Section 5). *A design document with nothing to report here has usually not met
  its hardware yet.*
- **Evaluation plan.** The measurements you will take (Section 9), each with its method and
  its target. Numbers you commit to now are twice as credible when you hit them later. And
  instructive either way.
- **Ownership map.** Which partner owns which subsystems (Section 10.1). Ownership means
  first authorship and answerability at the defense, not exclusivity.
- **AI-use plan.** What you'll use Claude Code for, what you won't, and how you'll keep the
  Section 3.3 boundary visible in your repository (e.g., the product source tree contains no
  network client but the LAN interface).

---

## 9. The Evaluation Report (M5)

**Adjectives are not measurements.** Your evaluation report (3–4 pages, submitted with the
final system) must contain, at minimum:

- **Latency or timing**, wherever your design claims it matters: distributions (not just
  means) for event-to-detection or sample-to-storage, measured under both idle and loaded
  CPU.
- **Resource footprint:** CPU utilization and RSS for each process, at steady state and over
  the full soak (the soak heartbeats give you this series for free; plot it).
- **One domain metric:** detection accuracy against ground truth you constructed, sustained
  sample rate with drop accounting, or query latency over the stored history. Pick the one
  your product lives or dies by.
- **Fault-injection results:** for each failure mode in your design-doc table, what you
  injected, what the system did, and the log excerpt proving it.
- **The mechanism comparisons your menu choices require** (e.g., interrupt vs. polling for
  item B, RT vs. default scheduling for item C), presented as experiments with method, data,
  and conclusion.
- **Limitations**, stated plainly, closing the loop on the constraints and substitutions
  declared in your design document (Section 5). *An honest limitations section is worth more
  at the defense than a suspiciously perfect results section, and we notice which one we are
  reading.*

Claude Code can generate plausible code. But it can't fake your understanding of your own
measurements. Which is why the defense draws so heavily on this report.

---

# Plan: car-ready tools, analysis helpers and M2 design-doc drafts, in one pass

## Context

M2 is due Wednesday 8 pm. Three M2 boxes need a real car: `firstcap` (real Mode 01
replies in a file), `baseline` (collection started) and `pidforester` (PID survey, protocol,
VIN). The OBDLink LX has arrived, but it is powered from OBD2 pin 16, so nothing can touch
it at the desk. This pass makes the car trip a single run-and-copy-out step: tested tools
(against a fake ELM327, never the real adapter), a drive runbook, analysis helpers for
afterward, and drafts of the design-doc sections the board still lists as open.

Camden's answers, taken as settled: tools first, then docs; logger runs on the Mac in
Python; JSONL logs; one branch, one draft PR, small commits; round-robin polling at the
adapter's maximum rate; optional GPS (off by default); session header and event lines;
VIN stored hashed; simulator = generic ELM327 plus scripted drive profile (no fault
injection); pyserial for logging, numpy and matplotlib for analysis; run to completion,
logging blockers as board items; one fresh-context review at the end; no owner split
between Camden and Lance (Lance is on the power supply, which is out of scope today).

## Ground rules this pass follows (CLAUDE.md)

- Branch `camden/m2/car-ready-tools` from freshly pulled `main` (pull already done, tree
  clean), created before the first edit. Draft PR opened at the first commit.
- Tests lead: each tool commit adds a test that failed first, in the same commit.
- One responsibility per commit, each building and passing on its own; stage explicit
  paths only; read every file in full before committing it.
- Every record and log line the sim writes carries `src=synth`; the logger writes
  `src=live`. No network code in `src/`; Python only in `tools/` (§2.5).
- Every decision I make is added to `docs/DECISIONS.md` as ⚠️ UNREVIEWED, in the same commit
  that implements it. I never lock a decision, tick a box or touch an issue by hand.
- Cross-area note: `CLAUDE.md` §6 still lists owners; I will not edit it, but I will say in
  the PR that the work crosses those lines by Camden's instruction.

## Work, in priority order (cut from the bottom if time runs out)

### Tier 1: car-ready

1. **`build`: tools environment.** `tools/requirements.txt` (pyserial), a
   `tools/requirements-analysis.txt` (numpy, matplotlib), a `tools/requirements-gps.txt`
   (pyobjc-framework-CoreLocation), `.gitignore` entries for `data/`, and a Makefile
   `toolcheck` target (stdlib `unittest`, tests in `tests/tools/`) wired into `make test`.
   It bootstraps `.venv` if missing, so a fresh clone stays green. Needs a look at
   `Makefile` `PY` selection (it already finds a Python with `tomllib`).
2. **`tools`: `tools/obdlib.py`**, the shared core. ELM327 framing and reply parsing
   (headers off, multi-line CAN replies, `NO DATA`, `?`, `BUFFER FULL`, `SEARCHING...`),
   Mode 01 decode table for the standard PIDs (formulas and units), support-bitmap
   decode, Mode 09 VIN decode, VIN hashing (sha256, first 12 hex; stated in the code as
   pseudonymization, not anonymity). Tests with the handout-standard worked examples,
   such as `41 0C 1A F8` is 1726 rpm.
3. **`tools`: `tools/obdsim.py`**, the `obdsim` board item. ELM327 emulator on a pty:
   `ATZ`, `ATE0`, `ATL0`, `ATH0`, `ATSP0`, `ATDP`, `ATRV`, `0100/0120/0140/0160`, Mode 01
   PIDs, `0902` VIN, timing close to a Bluetooth adapter. A scripted drive profile (idle,
   accelerate, cruise, decel, stop) drives RPM, speed, load, coolant, intake, MAP,
   throttle and fuel trims from one simple vehicle model. Writes `src=synth` into any
   record it creates. Tests: command table and profile continuity. No fault injection.
4. **`tools`: `tools/pidscan.py`**, replacing the stub. Opens the port, runs
   `ATZ/ATE0/ATSP0`, walks `0100/0120/0140/0160`, prints a table of supported PIDs with
   names, `ATDP`, `ATRV`, and the VIN (shown on the terminal, the file keeps only the
   hash). Writes `data/pidscan-<date>.json` plus a markdown block for
   `docs/hardware/pid-survey.md`. Tested against the sim.
5. **`tools`: `tools/obdlog.py`**, the drive logger. One command:
   `tools/obdlog.py --port /dev/cu.OBDLinkLX* --out data/`. Behavior:
   - session header line (tool version, adapter `ATZ` string, protocol, supported PIDs,
     VIN hash, host name, wall and monotonic start);
   - round-robin poll of every supported PID, as fast as the adapter replies;
   - one JSONL line per reply: `src`, `seq`, `t_mono`, `t_wall`, `pid`, `raw`, `val`,
     `unit`; bad or missing replies become `event` lines, never silent drops;
   - append-only, fsync every N lines or 1 s (whichever first), clean footer on
     Ctrl-C / SIGTERM; reconnect with exponential backoff on a drop, logged as events;
   - a one-line status every few seconds (lines, req/s, per-PID rate, last event);
   - `--gps` optional: CoreLocation via pyobjc, GPS lines under their own type; if the
     library or permission is missing, one `event` line and logging continues;
   - `--sim` shortcut that starts `obdsim` so the whole path can be rehearsed.
   Tests: drive against the sim, kill the pty master mid-run to test reconnect, torn last

order, and only records whose batch has been committed to disk. "Committed" means
durable, not merely written: a reader of the file sees a `COMMIT` in the page cache before
`fsync` returns, so `storaged` publishes a **durable offset** only after `fsync` returns,
and `analyzed` never reads past it. `obdctl` and the status page never read samples
themselves; they ask the supervisor over its Unix socket, and the supervisor asks the
process that holds the answer.

**Why.** An SPSC ring has one consumer, so the old diagram could not be built as drawn.
Camden chose this over two rings, 2026-10-21:

- the ring stays truly single-producer, single-consumer, which B.3 and its tests assume;
- `analyzed` learns only from what is durable, so a baseline never absorbs a sample that
  a power cut later erased;
- rebuilding baselines after a crash reads the same log through the same code as live
  analysis, so recovery is not a second implementation to test;
- `analyzed` can crash or restart without losing input: it resumes from where it last
  read.

`fsync`), which is nothing for signals that move over minutes. `analyzed` depends on the
log format, so a format change touches both processes. If `storaged` is down, analysis

content.content:
330	(`keyoff`, `cranklog`, `expshut`).
331	
332	### A.7 — Standard Mode 01 requests are the primary data path ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
333	
334	`D-012` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
335	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
336	
337	*Revised 2026-09-21 by D-015, before any review: the CAN-level detail (arbitration IDs,
338	broadcast frames, a listen-only flag, the port-traffic check) went with the MCP2515.*
339	
340	**Decision.** The capture daemon gets its signals by sending **standard OBD2 Mode 01
341	requests** through the OBD2 adapter (D-019) on a fixed, rate-limited, round-robin schedule,
342	one request outstanding at a time. Every timeout and every unanswered PID is logged.
343	
344	**Why.** D-011 (now D-024) makes this a plug-in device, and the thing that makes a plug-in
345	device work on a car it has never seen is the part of the protocol every car must speak:
346	Mode 01 is mandatory on US cars from model year 1996. *"Learns this car's normal"* is
347	precisely what lets one device serve different cars without per-model decode work: it
348	never needs to know what normal *is* ahead of time.
349	
350	**Sample-rate consequence.** Signals are round-robined, so each PID is sampled at
351	(request rate ÷ PID count) — on the order of 1 Hz each for a ~10 requests/s budget over
352	~8 PIDs. That is ample for what we watch (warm-up over minutes, fuel trim against load,
353	drift over days) and must be stated in `docs/DESIGN.md` §4. The request budget itself
354	is a design-doc number to justify, not a constant to pick.
355	
356	**Cost.** The device sends requests to the car's ECU. Kept safe by the rate limit, one
357	outstanding request, and only standard read-only Mode 01 requests — the same thing every
358	scan tool does.
359	
360	**Scope note.** "Works on any car" is the product's direction, not our claim. The claim is
361	E.1 (D-021): one car, a learned normal, fault areas named, measured error rates.
362	
363	### A.8 — A real-time clock keeps wall time while the box is off ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
364	
365	`D-030` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
366	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
367	
368	**Decision.** The box gets a small real-time clock module on the Pi's I2C bus, kept
369	running by its own backup cell or capacitor while the box is off. At boot the system
370	clock is set from it. If the clock reports its time as invalid (its backup was lost),
371	that session's wall time is marked untrusted. Every record still carries `mono_ns`
372	regardless. The phone page stays read-only: it does not set the clock.
373	
374	**Why.** The Pi has no battery-backed clock, and the box has no network (`CLAUDE.md`
375	§2.3). Raspberry Pi OS's `fake-hwclock` restores the time saved at the last shutdown, so
376	the clock does not advance while the box is off, and every boot would appear to follow the
377	previous shutdown directly. The soak (D-023) must prove a 48-hour wall-clock span across
378	parked gaps, and the report's session list needs real times. Camden chose the clock
379	module, 2026-10-21, over the phone setting the time (that depends on someone opening the
380	page on every drive) and over no wall clock at all (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.2, R5).
381	
382	**Cost.**
383	
384	- One more part, on I2C (GPIO2 and GPIO3, header pins 3 and 5), drawn in the Pi interface
385	  block, and bought only after the design is signed.
386	- Its backup cell or capacitor lives in a parked car's cabin, so its temperature rating
387	  must cover that, checked against the part's datasheet (`rtcspec`).
388	- A clock that has drifted or lost its backup must be detected rather than trusted, so the
389	  boot path checks it (`rtcboot`).
390	
391	---
392	
393	## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms
394	
395	### B.1 — Mechanism commitments: D and E; B and F only with a Pi-side sensor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
396	
397	`D-017` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
398	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
399	· **Supersedes:** D-002 (§G.3)
400	
401	*B and F declined 2026-10-21 by D-029 (§B.7), before any review: no Pi-side sensor will be
402	added, so D and E are the committed pair and the "only if" rows below no longer apply.*
403	
404	The handout requires two, implemented by us and measured.
405	
406	| Mechanism | Status | Where |
407	| --- | --- | --- |
408	| **D** — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent | **committed** | `src/store/` |
409	| **E** — multi-process with a supervisor | **committed** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` |
410	| **B** — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison | declined (D-029) | — |
411	| **F** — high-rate no-drop SPSC ring | declined (D-029) | — |
412	| **A**, **C**, raw CAN | stretch, after D and E are measured | — |
413	
414	**D.** *Power disappears every time the key turns off* (D-024). The box shuts down
415	cleanly on its supercapacitor when it can, but the bank is empty at a cold start, a
416	pulled cable beats it, and a crank dip can reset the Pi, so storage must survive a cut at
417	any instant. *(Revised 2026-10-21 by D-024; it read "we never get a clean shutdown".)*
418	Measured by cutting the Pi's own 5 V rail mid-write, after the converter so the
419	supercapacitor cannot cover it, repeatedly, and proving recovery (`expcrash`). Pulling
420	the charger no longer tests this: it triggers a clean shutdown.
421	
422	**E.** A recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on
423	duty. Any child may be `kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers. Measured by killing
424	each child repeatedly and timing detection and recovery (`expkill`).
425	
426	**Why B and F left the OBD data path (D-015, D-019).** B needs an interrupt that *our*
427	design services. The adapter's interrupts belong to the kernel's Bluetooth and RFCOMM
428	stack; our process only blocks on a tty, and at ~10–20 replies/s a poll loop keeps up
429	trivially — the comparison would measure the tty layer, not a design of ours. F needs a
430	*high-rate* stream; ~10–20 samples/s never stresses a ring, so "zero drops under
431	contention" would be true and meaningless.
432	
433	**What brings them back.** An MPU-6050 on the Pi's I2C, its `INT` pin on a GPIO: kHz
434	samples from a hardware FIFO give a real interrupt-vs-polling comparison (B) and a rate
435	that stresses the ring (F). That was board item `pisensor`; D-029 declined it.
436	
437	**The ring stays regardless.** It is how capture hands samples to storage across the
438	process boundary E requires, and B.3 still binds it.

    """
    return hashlib.sha256(vin.encode("ascii")).hexdigest()[:12]

    0x07: ("Long term fuel trim, bank 1", "%", 1, lambda d: (d[0] - 128) * 100 / 128),
    0x08: ("Short term fuel trim, bank 2", "%", 1, lambda d: (d[0] - 128) * 100 / 128),
    0x09: ("Long term fuel trim, bank 2", "%", 1, lambda d: (d[0] - 128) * 100 / 128),
    0x0A: ("Fuel pressure", "kPa", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 3),
    0x0B: ("Intake manifold pressure", "kPa", 1, lambda d: d[0]),
    0x0C: ("Engine speed", "rpm", 2, lambda d: _u16(d) / 4),
    0x0D: ("Vehicle speed", "km/h", 1, lambda d: d[0]),
    0x0E: ("Timing advance", "deg", 1, lambda d: d[0] / 2 - 64),
    0x0F: ("Intake air temperature", "degC", 1, lambda d: d[0] - 40),
    0x10: ("Mass air flow", "g/s", 2, lambda d: _u16(d) / 100),
    0x11: ("Throttle position", "%", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 100 / 255),
    0x1F: ("Run time since start", "s", 2, _u16),
    0x21: ("Distance with MIL on", "km", 2, _u16),
    0x2C: ("Commanded EGR", "%", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 100 / 255),
    0x2F: ("Fuel level", "%", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 100 / 255),
    0x30: ("Warm-ups since codes cleared", "count", 1, lambda d: d[0]),
    0x31: ("Distance since codes cleared", "km", 2, _u16),
    0x33: ("Barometric pressure", "kPa", 1, lambda d: d[0]),
    0x42: ("Control module voltage", "V", 2, lambda d: _u16(d) / 1000),
    0x43: ("Absolute load", "%", 2, lambda d: _u16(d) * 100 / 255),
    0x44: ("Commanded equivalence ratio", "ratio", 2, lambda d: _u16(d) / 32768),
    0x45: ("Relative throttle position", "%", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 100 / 255),
    0x46: ("Ambient air temperature", "degC", 1, lambda d: d[0] - 40),
    0x47: ("Absolute throttle position B", "%", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 100 / 255),
    0x49: ("Accelerator pedal position D", "%", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 100 / 255),
    0x4A: ("Accelerator pedal position E", "%", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 100 / 255),
    0x4C: ("Commanded throttle actuator", "%", 1, lambda d: d[0] * 100 / 255),
    0x5C: ("Engine oil temperature", "degC", 1, lambda d: d[0] - 40),
    0x5E: ("Engine fuel rate", "L/h", 2, lambda d: _u16(d) / 20),

# Wide-band O2 sensors 0x24-0x2B report the equivalence ratio first.

    PIDS[_pid] = (f"Catalyst temperature {_label}", "degC", 2, lambda d: _u16(d) / 10 - 40)

    entry = PIDS.get(pid)
    return entry[0] if entry else f"PID {pid:02X}"


def decode(pid, data):
    """(value, unit) for a Mode 01 reply's data bytes; (None, '') if unknown or short."""
    entry = PIDS.get(pid)
    if entry is None or len(data) < entry[2]:
        return (None, "")
    return (float(entry[3](data)), entry[1])


def support_pids(base, data):
    """The PIDs a support-bitmap reply (PID 0x00, 0x20, ...) lists as supported.

    The most significant bit is PID base+1 and the least significant is base+0x20, which
    says whether the next block exists.
    """
    if len(data) != 4:
        raise AdapterError(f"support bitmap needs 4 bytes, got {len(data)}")
    bits = int.from_bytes(data, "big")
    return {base + 1 + i for i in range(32) if bits & (1 << (31 - i))}


def decode_vin(raw):
    """The VIN from a Mode 09 PID 02 reply, multi-frame or one frame per line."""
    chunks = []
    framed = {}
    for line in _lines(raw):
        _check_text(line)
        m = re.match(r"^(\d+):\s*(.*)$", line)
        if m:
            data = _hex_bytes(m.group(2))
            if data is not None:
                framed[int(m.group(1))] = data
            continue
        data = _hex_bytes(line)
        if data is not None and len(data) >= 3 and data[:2] == b"\x49\x02":
            chunks.append((data[2], data[3:]))
    if framed:
        body = b"".join(framed[k] for k in sorted(framed))
        body = body[3:] if body[:2] == b"\x49\x02" else body
    elif chunks:
        body = b"".join(c for _, c in sorted(chunks))
    else:
        raise AdapterError("no VIN in reply")
    vin = body.replace(b"\x00", b"").decode("ascii", errors="replace").strip()
    if not vin:
        raise AdapterError("empty VIN")
    return vin


def vin_hash(vin):
    """A short stable label that groups sessions by car without writing the VIN down.

    This is pseudonymization, not anonymity: a VIN has little entropy, so anyone holding
    candidate VINs can check them against it. It keeps the VIN out of files and git.
    """
    return hashlib.sha256(vin.encode("ascii")).hexdigest()[:12]

"""obdsim: a fake ELM327 on a pty. Everything it says is synthetic."""
import os
import tempfile
import time
import unittest

import obdlib
import obdsim
import serial


def ask(sim, cmd, t=10.0):
    return sim.handle(cmd, t)


class Commands(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.sim = obdsim.Simulator()

    def test_reset_names_itself_as_a_simulator(self):
        reply = ask(self.sim, "ATZ")
        self.assertIn("ELM327", reply)
        self.assertIn("SIM", reply)
        self.assertTrue(reply.endswith(">"))

    def test_echo_is_on_until_ate0(self):
        self.assertTrue(ask(self.sim, "ATRV").startswith("ATRV\r"))
        self.assertTrue(ask(self.sim, "ATE0").endswith("OK\r\r>"))
        self.assertFalse(ask(self.sim, "ATRV").startswith("ATRV"))

    def test_settings_commands_say_ok(self):
        for cmd in ("ATE0", "ATL0", "ATH0", "ATS1", "ATSP0", "ATST64", "ATAT1"):
            with self.subTest(cmd=cmd):
                self.assertIn("OK", ask(self.sim, cmd))

    def test_protocol_and_voltage(self):
        ask(self.sim, "ATE0")
        self.assertIn("ISO 15765-4", ask(self.sim, "ATDP"))
        self.assertRegex(ask(self.sim, "ATRV"), r"\d+\.\dV")

    def test_garbage_gets_a_question_mark(self):
        ask(self.sim, "ATE0")
        self.assertEqual(ask(self.sim, "ZZZZ"), "?\r\r>")

    def test_first_obd_request_shows_the_searching_banner_once(self):
        ask(self.sim, "ATE0")
        ask(self.sim, "ATSP0")
        self.assertIn("SEARCHING...", ask(self.sim, "0100"))
        self.assertNotIn("SEARCHING...", ask(self.sim, "0100"))

    def test_reset_clears_the_banner_state(self):
        ask(self.sim, "ATE0")
        ask(self.sim, "0100")
        ask(self.sim, "ATZ")
        ask(self.sim, "ATE0")
        self.assertIn("SEARCHING...", ask(self.sim, "0100"))


class ModeOne(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.sim = obdsim.Simulator()
        ask(self.sim, "ATE0")
        ask(self.sim, "0100")   # consume the banner

    def supported(self):
        found, base = set(), 0x00
        while True:
            reply = ask(self.sim, obdlib.request(1, base))
            block = obdlib.support_pids(base, obdlib.parse_response(reply, 1, base))
            found |= block
            if base + 0x20 not in block:
                return found
            base += 0x20

    def test_support_chain_lists_every_modelled_pid(self):
        self.assertEqual({p for p in self.supported() if p % 0x20}, set(obdsim.MODELLED))

    def test_values_round_trip_through_the_decoder(self):
        t = 75.0
        state = obdsim.vehicle_state(t)
        for pid in obdsim.MODELLED:
            with self.subTest(pid=hex(pid)):
                reply = self.sim.handle(obdlib.request(1, pid), t)
                data = obdlib.parse_response(reply, 1, pid)
                value, _unit = obdlib.decode(pid, data)
                self.assertAlmostEqual(value, state[pid], delta=max(1.0, abs(state[pid]) * 0.02))

    def test_unmodelled_pid_has_no_data(self):
        with self.assertRaises(obdlib.NoData):
            obdlib.parse_response(ask(self.sim, "015C"), 1, 0x5C)

    def test_vin_is_multiframe_and_decodes(self):
        vin = obdlib.decode_vin(ask(self.sim, "0902"))
        self.assertEqual(vin, obdsim.SIM_VIN)
        self.assertEqual(len(vin), 17)

    def test_mode_nine_support(self):
        data = obdlib.parse_response(ask(self.sim, "0900"), 9, 0x00)
        self.assertIn(0x02, obdlib.support_pids(0x00, data))


class DriveProfile(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_phases_cover_idle_acceleration_cruise_and_stop(self):
        speeds = [obdsim.vehicle_state(t)[0x0D] for t in range(0, 140)]
        self.assertEqual(speeds[5], 0)
        self.assertGreater(max(speeds), 70)
        self.assertEqual(speeds[130], 0)

    def test_signals_are_continuous(self):
        prev = obdsim.vehicle_state(0.0)
        for i in range(1, 2800):
            cur = obdsim.vehicle_state(i * 0.05)
            self.assertLess(abs(cur[0x0D] - prev[0x0D]), 3.0, f"speed jumps at {i * 0.05}")
            self.assertLess(abs(cur[0x05] - prev[0x05]), 0.5, f"coolant jumps at {i * 0.05}")
            prev = cur

    def test_engine_warms_up(self):
        self.assertLess(obdsim.vehicle_state(0)[0x05], 40)
        self.assertGreater(obdsim.vehicle_state(1200)[0x05], 85)

    def test_values_stay_inside_their_pid_range(self):
        for t in range(0, 1500, 7):
            s = obdsim.vehicle_state(float(t))
            self.assertTrue(0 <= s[0x04] <= 100)
            self.assertTrue(0 <= s[0x11] <= 100)
            self.assertTrue(-100 <= s[0x06] <= 99)
            self.assertTrue(600 <= s[0x0C] <= 6000)


class PtyServer(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_serial_client_talks_to_the_sim_through_a_link(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            link = os.path.join(d, "obd")
            with obdsim.PtyServer(link=link, latency=0.0):
                port = serial.Serial(link, 38400, timeout=2)
                try:
                    port.write(b"ATZ\r")
                    buf = b""
                    deadline = time.monotonic() + 3
                    while not buf.endswith(b">") and time.monotonic() < deadline:
                        buf += port.read(64)
                    self.assertIn(b"ELM327", buf)
                finally:
                    port.close()
            self.assertFalse(os.path.lexists(link), "link is removed when the sim stops")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

cat > tools/pidscan.py <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mode 01 supported-PID survey. Closes D-007's question for one car (board: pidforester).

Run it parked, engine running, with the OBDLink LX paired (D-019):

    tools/pidscan.py --port /dev/cu.OBDLinkLX-SPP     # Mac (check `ls /dev/cu.*`)
    tools/pidscan.py --port /dev/obd                  # Pi

It prints the adapter, the protocol, the battery voltage, the VIN (on screen only) and
every supported PID with one live reading, then writes data/pidscan-<time>.json and a
markdown block to paste into docs/hardware/pid-survey.md. Files carry the VIN's hash,
never the VIN itself.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import json
import os
import sys

import elm
import obdlib

# VIN position 10 encodes the model year on a 30-year cycle (I, O, Q, U, Z, 0 unused).
_YEAR_CODES = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTVWXY123456789"


def model_year(vin, now=None):
    """The most recent model year the VIN's 10th character can mean, or None."""
    if len(vin) != 17 or vin[9].upper() not in _YEAR_CODES:
        return None
    now = now or datetime.date.today().year
    year = 1980 + _YEAR_CODES.index(vin[9].upper())
    while year + 30 <= now + 1:
        year += 30
    return year


def scan(ad):
    """Survey one adapter session. The VIN is returned separately and never stored."""
    banner = ad.init()
    result = {
        "src": "synth" if ad.is_sim else "live",
        "t_wall": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "adapter": banner,
        "protocol": ad.protocol(),
        "voltage": ad.voltage(),
        "vin_hash": None,
        "model_year": None,
        "supported": [],
        "samples": {},
    }
    vin = None
    try:
        vin = ad.vin()
        result["vin_hash"] = obdlib.vin_hash(vin)
        result["model_year"] = model_year(vin)
    except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
        result["vin_error"] = str(e)
    for pid in sorted(ad.supported_pids()):
        key = f"{pid:02X}"
        result["supported"].append(key)
        try:
            data = ad.query(1, pid)
            value, unit = obdlib.decode(pid, data)
            result["samples"][key] = {"raw": data.hex(" ").upper(), "val": value,
                                      "unit": unit, "name": obdlib.pid_name(pid)}
        except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
            result["samples"][key] = {"error": str(e), "name": obdlib.pid_name(pid)}
    return result, vin


def render_markdown(r):
    lines = [
        f"### Survey {r['t_wall'][:19]}Z (`src={r['src']}`)",
        "",
        f"- Adapter: `{r['adapter']}`",
        f"- Protocol (`ATDP`): `{r['protocol']}`",
        f"- Battery (`ATRV`): `{r['voltage']}`",
        f"- VIN hash: `{r['vin_hash']}`; model year from VIN: {r['model_year']}",
        f"- Supported Mode 01 PIDs ({len(r['supported'])}): "
        + ", ".join(f"`{p}`" for p in r["supported"]),
        "",
        "| PID | Signal | Raw | Value |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for key in r["supported"]:
        s = r["samples"][key]
        value = s.get("error") or (f"{s['val']:.2f} {s['unit']}" if s["val"] is not None
                                   else "(not decoded)")
        lines.append(f"| 0x{key} | {s['name']} | `{s.get('raw', '')}` | {value} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--port", required=True, help="adapter serial port")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data", help="directory for the survey files")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        ad = elm.Adapter(args.port)
    except elm.LinkLost as e:
        print(f"pidscan: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The drive logger: poll every supported Mode 01 PID and append each reply to JSONL.

    tools/obdlog.py --port /dev/cu.OBDLinkLX-SPP        # Mac, a real drive
    tools/obdlog.py --sim                               # rehearsal against obdsim

One file per session, data/drive-<time>-<src>.jsonl, one JSON object per line:

    header  adapter, protocol, battery, VIN hash, PID list, tool and schema version
    sample  src, seq, t_mono, t_wall, pid, raw hex, decoded val, unit
    event   no_data, timeout, adapter_error, reinit, pid_absent, link_lost,
            reconnected, gps_unavailable, gps_error, ...
    gps     a Mac location fix, only with --gps
    footer  why the session ended, and its counts

Every line carries `src`: `live` for the car, `synth` when the adapter is obdsim
(CLAUDE.md 2.7). Writes are append-only and fsync'd every --fsync-lines lines or
--fsync-sec seconds, so a crash or a closed lid loses at most that much. A Bluetooth
drop is logged and retried with backoff; the logger only stops on Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or
--max-seconds. This is a tool for collecting data (D-033), not the product's obdd.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import json
import os
import signal
import socket
import sys
import time

import elm
import obdlib

TOOL = "obdlog 1"
SCHEMA = 1
NO_DATA_LIMIT = 5        # consecutive NO DATA before a PID is set aside as absent
ABSENT_RETRY_SEC = 60.0  # how often an absent PID is tried again
ERROR_LIMIT = 3          # consecutive timeouts or adapter errors before a reset


def _wall():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds")


class LogWriter:
    """Append-only JSONL with periodic fsync. Every line gets src, seq and timestamps."""

    def __init__(self, path, src, fsync_lines, fsync_sec):
        self.path, self.src = path, src
        self.fsync_lines, self.fsync_sec = fsync_lines, fsync_sec
        self.f = open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8")
        self.seq = 0
        self.unsynced = 0
        self.last_sync = time.monotonic()
        dfd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
        try:
            os.fsync(dfd)        # the new file's directory entry survives a crash too
        finally:
            os.close(dfd)

    def write(self, rtype, **fields):
        rec = {"type": rtype, "src": self.src, "seq": self.seq,
               "t_mono": round(time.monotonic(), 4), "t_wall": _wall()}
        rec.update(fields)
        self.f.write(json.dumps(rec, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
        self.seq += 1
        self.unsynced += 1
        if (self.unsynced >= self.fsync_lines
                or time.monotonic() - self.last_sync >= self.fsync_sec):
            self.sync()

    def sync(self):
        self.f.flush()
        os.fsync(self.f.fileno())
        self.unsynced = 0
        self.last_sync = time.monotonic()

    def close(self):
        self.sync()
        self.f.close()


def read_log(path):
    """(records, torn): every complete line, and whether a torn last line was dropped."""
    records, torn = [], False
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        lines = f.read().split("\n")
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            records.append(json.loads(line))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            if i == len(lines) - 1:
                torn = True       # the last line was mid-write when the session ended
            else:
                raise
    return records, torn


class Stop:
    def __init__(self):
        self.reason = None

    def __call__(self, signum, _frame):
        self.reason = "sigint" if signum == signal.SIGINT else "sigterm"


def connect(path, tries, backoff_min, stop, log=None):
    """Open and init the adapter, retrying with exponential backoff. None if stopped."""
    delay, attempt = backoff_min, 0
    while stop.reason is None and (tries <= 0 or attempt < tries):
        attempt += 1
        ad = None
        try:
            ad = elm.Adapter(path)
            ad.init()
            return ad, attempt
        except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e:
            if ad:
                ad.close()
            if log:
                log("connect_failed", attempt=attempt, detail=str(e))
            print(f"obdlog: connect attempt {attempt} failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            if tries > 0 and attempt >= tries:
                break
            end = time.monotonic() + delay
            while stop.reason is None and time.monotonic() < end:
                time.sleep(0.05)
            delay = min(delay * 2, 30.0)
    return None, attempt


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--port", help="adapter serial port (/dev/cu.* on a Mac, /dev/obd)")
    ap.add_argument("--sim", action="store_true", help="start obdsim and log from it")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data", help="directory for session files")
    ap.add_argument("--pids", help="comma-separated hex PIDs; default: all supported")
    ap.add_argument("--gps", action="store_true", help="also log Mac location (optional)")
    ap.add_argument("--fsync-lines", type=int, default=50)
    ap.add_argument("--fsync-sec", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--status-sec", type=float, default=5.0)
    ap.add_argument("--max-seconds", type=float, default=0, help="stop after this long")
    ap.add_argument("--connect-tries", type=int, default=0,
                    help="attempts at the first connection; 0 = keep trying")
    ap.add_argument("--backoff-min", type=float, default=1.0, help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if bool(args.port) == bool(args.sim):
        ap.error("give exactly one of --port or --sim")
    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)

    stop = Stop()
    old = {s: signal.getsignal(s) for s in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM)}
    if threading_is_main():
        for s in old:
            signal.signal(s, stop)
    sim = None
    try:
        if args.sim:
            import obdsim  # noqa: PLC0415 - only needed for rehearsals
            sim = obdsim.PtyServer(link=os.path.join(args.out, "obd-sim")).__enter__()
            args.port = sim.link
        return _run(args, stop)
    finally:
        if sim:
            sim.__exit__(None, None, None)
        if threading_is_main():
            for s, h in old.items():
                signal.signal(s, h)


def threading_is_main():
    import threading  # noqa: PLC0415
    return threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread()


def _run(args, stop):
    t_start = time.monotonic()
    deadline = t_start + args.max_seconds if args.max_seconds else None

    def expired():
        return deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline

    ad, _ = connect(args.port, args.connect_tries or 0, args.backoff_min, stop)
    if ad is None:
        print(f"obdlog: could not connect to {args.port}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    src = "synth" if (ad.is_sim or args.sim) else "live"
    try:
        supported = ad.supported_pids()
        vin = None
        try:
            vin = ad.vin()
        except obdlib.AdapterError:
            pass
        header = {"tool": TOOL, "schema": SCHEMA, "host": socket.gethostname(),
                  "port": args.port, "adapter": ad.banner, "protocol": ad.protocol(),
                  "voltage": ad.voltage(),
                  "vin_hash": obdlib.vin_hash(vin) if vin else None,
                  "supported": [f"{p:02X}" for p in sorted(supported)]}
    except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e:
        ad.close()
        print(f"obdlog: session setup failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    pids = ([int(p, 16) for p in args.pids.split(",")] if args.pids
            else sorted(supported))
    header["pids"] = [f"{p:02X}" for p in pids]

    stamp = _wall()[:19].replace(":", "").replace("-", "")
    path = os.path.join(args.out, f"drive-{stamp}-{src}.jsonl")
    out = LogWriter(path, src, args.fsync_lines, args.fsync_sec)
    out.write("header", **header)

    counts = {"samples": 0, "events": 0, "gps": 0}
    last_event = ["none"]

    def event(name, **fields):
        counts["events"] += 1
        last_event[0] = name + (f" {fields['pid']}" if "pid" in fields else "")
        out.write("event", event=name, **fields)

    gps = None
    if args.gps:
        import macgps  # noqa: PLC0415 - optional
        try:
            gps = macgps.start()
        except macgps.GpsUnavailable as e:
            event("gps_unavailable", detail=str(e))

    no_data = {p: 0 for p in pids}
    absent = {}                       # pid -> monotonic time it was set aside
    errors = 0
    next_status = time.monotonic() + args.status_sec
    print(f"obdlog: logging {len(pids)} PIDs to {path} (src={src}); Ctrl-C to stop",
          file=sys.stderr)

    try:
        while stop.reason is None and not expired():
            for pid in pids:
                if stop.reason is not None or expired():
                    break
                key = f"{pid:02X}"
                now = time.monotonic()
                if pid in absent:
                    if now - absent[pid] < ABSENT_RETRY_SEC:
                        continue
                    absent[pid] = now
                try:
                    data = ad.query(1, pid)
                except obdlib.NoData:
                    no_data[pid] += 1
                    event("no_data", pid=key)
                    if no_data[pid] == NO_DATA_LIMIT and pid not in absent:
                        absent[pid] = now
                        event("pid_absent", pid=key, after=NO_DATA_LIMIT)
                    continue
                except elm.LinkLost as e:
                    event("link_lost", detail=str(e))
                    ad.close()
                    ad, attempts = connect(args.port, 0, args.backoff_min, stop,
                                           log=lambda n, **f: event(n, **f))
                    if ad is None:
                        break
                    event("reconnected", attempts=attempts)
                    errors = 0
                    break
                except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
                    errors += 1
                    event("timeout" if isinstance(e, elm.Timeout) else "adapter_error",
                          pid=key, detail=str(e))
                    if errors >= ERROR_LIMIT:
                        errors = 0
                        try:
                            event("reinit", banner=ad.init())
                        except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e2:
                            event("reinit_failed", detail=str(e2))
                    continue
                errors = 0
                no_data[pid] = 0
                if pid in absent:
                    del absent[pid]
                    event("pid_present", pid=key)
                value, unit = obdlib.decode(pid, data)
                out.write("sample", pid=key, raw=data.hex(" ").upper(), val=value,
                          unit=unit)
                counts["samples"] += 1

                if gps is not None:
                    fixes, err = gps.poll()
                    for fix in fixes:
                        out.write("gps", **fix)
                        counts["gps"] += 1
                    if err:
                        event("gps_error", detail=err)

                if time.monotonic() >= next_status:
                    el = time.monotonic() - t_start
                    print(f"[{int(el) // 60:02d}:{int(el) % 60:02d}] "
                          f"{counts['samples']} samples, "
                          f"{counts['samples'] / el:.1f}/s, {counts['events']} events "
                          f"(last: {last_event[0]}), gps {counts['gps']}",
                          file=sys.stderr)
                    next_status += args.status_sec
            if ad is None:
                break
    finally:
        reason = stop.reason or ("max_seconds" if expired() else "link_gave_up")
        out.write("footer", reason=reason, seconds=round(time.monotonic() - t_start, 3),
                  **counts)
        out.close()
        if ad is not None:
            ad.close()
        if gps is not None:
            gps.stop()
    print(f"obdlog: {counts['samples']} samples, {counts['events']} events -> {path}",
          file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

4. reports source-present on a GPIO;
5. cuts the Pi's supply when the Pi signals halt-done, even if the source has returned,
   then re-enables after a short off time;
6. powers on again by itself when the source returns.

**Not supported:** a charger that stays live with the key off. The box would stay on.

An undervolted Pi keeps running and corrupts the SD card later. Prove the supply; do not
trust its label.

### Measurements (dated; a row without a result has not been done)

| Measurement | How | Feeds | Date | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Does the owner's charger go dead with the key off? Is it live in accessory? | USB-C meter, key off / ACC / run | `keyoff` | | |
| Supply dip at crank | meter or scope at the charger's output | `cranklog`, the grace period | | |
| Pi 4 draw by state: boot, idle, loaded, shutdown | USB-C meter | `powerspec` | | |
| Boot time and shutdown time on the real image | `systemd-analyze`, log timestamps | `bootbudget` | | |
| Bank discharge into a dummy load; charge time from empty | meter, stopwatch | `capbench` | | |
| `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start | on the Pi; must be `0x0` | `keyoff` | | |
| Pi and bank temperature in a sealed shell, hot cabin | Pi sensor, thermometer | `thermal` | | |
| Dongle key-off current from pin 16 | meter | `dongledrain` | | |

## Before leaving the house

1. Set up the tools once (needs the network):

   ```sh
   make toolcheck          # builds .venv with pyserial and runs the tool tests
   ```

2. Rehearse the whole path against the simulator:

   ```sh
   PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/obdlog.py --sim --max-seconds 20
   ```

   It should report about 20 samples per second and write
   `data/drive-<time>-synth.jsonl`.
3. Charge the laptop. Optional: `pip install -r tools/requirements-gps.txt` into the
   venv for `--gps`, then run the rehearsal once with `--gps` so macOS asks for the
   location permission at the desk, not in the car.
4. Turn off sleep for the drive: run the logger under `caffeinate -i` (below).

## In the car, parked (about 10 minutes)

1. Plug the LX into the OBD2 port, under the dash on the driver's side. Start the engine.
2. Pair it: System Settings, Bluetooth. If it does not show up, check the quick-start
   card in the box for how the LX enters pairing mode.
3. Find its serial port:

   ```sh
   ls /dev/cu.*
   ```

   Record the name here. If no new `/dev/cu.*` appears after pairing, the Mac route has
   failed: use the Pi (last section).
4. Survey, engine idling:

   ```sh
   PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/pidscan.py --port /dev/cu.<name>
   ```

   It prints the protocol, the battery voltage, the VIN (on screen only) and one reading
   per supported PID, and writes `data/pidscan-<time>-live.{json,md}`. If it hangs at
   the start, the adapter is still searching for the protocol; give it 15 s.

## The drive

```sh
caffeinate -i env PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/obdlog.py \
    --port /dev/cu.<name>            # add --gps if it was set up
```

- Start it parked, engine running. It needs no input; a status line prints every 5 s.
- A passenger watches the status line, or nobody does. Never the driver.
- Drive a mix: a cold start if possible, idle, town, a highway stretch, a stop.
- Ctrl-C ends the session cleanly. A closed lid or a crash loses at most a second.
- A Bluetooth drop shows as `link_lost` and the logger reconnects by itself.

## Afterward

1. Check the capture: `PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/obdsum.py data/drive-*.jsonl`
   (rates, gaps, events per PID).
2. Paste the survey's markdown block, from `data/pidscan-*-live.md`, into
   `docs/hardware/pid-survey.md` under the Forester column.
3. Keep the full logs out of git (`data/` is ignored). Commit a short excerpt as
   evidence in its own commit, with the `obdsum` output.
4. Tick `pidforester`, `firstcap` and `baseline` yourself when they are true, then run
   `python3 tools/board_sync.py`.

## If the Mac cannot see the adapter: use the Pi

On the Pi, with the car running and the LX in the port:

```sh
bluetoothctl            # then: power on, scan on, pair <MAC>, trust <MAC>, quit
sudo rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1
ls -l /dev/rfcomm0
```

Then run the same two commands with `--port /dev/rfcomm0`. Record the MAC address in
`docs/hardware/wiring.md`.

## Results

| Date | Port name | Survey file | Drive file | Samples/s | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | | | | | |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Summarize drive logs from obdlog: session length, rates, gaps and events per PID.

    tools/obdsum.py data/drive-*.jsonl

This is the first evidence for `firstcap`: how many replies each PID gave, how often,
the longest gap, and what went wrong.
"""
import argparse
import statistics
import sys

import obdlib
import obdlog


def summarize(records):
    srcs = {r["src"] for r in records}
    if len(srcs) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"one session must have one src, found {sorted(srcs)}")
    header = next((r for r in records if r["type"] == "header"), {})
    footer = next((r for r in records if r["type"] == "footer"), None)
    samples = [r for r in records if r["type"] == "sample"]
    t = [r["t_mono"] for r in records if r["type"] in ("sample", "event")]
    seconds = (max(t) - min(t)) if len(t) > 1 else 0.0

    pids, events = {}, {}
    for r in samples:
        p = pids.setdefault(r["pid"], {"vals": [], "times": [], "unit": r.get("unit", ""),
                                       "no_data": 0, "errors": 0})
        p["times"].append(r["t_mono"])
        if r.get("val") is not None:
            p["vals"].append(r["val"])
    for r in records:
        if r["type"] != "event":
            continue
        events[r["event"]] = events.get(r["event"], 0) + 1
        if "pid" in r:
            p = pids.setdefault(r["pid"], {"vals": [], "times": [], "unit": "",
                                           "no_data": 0, "errors": 0})
            p["no_data" if r["event"] == "no_data" else "errors"] += 1

    out = {}
    for key, p in sorted(pids.items()):
        times, vals = p["times"], p["vals"]
        gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(times, times[1:])]
        out[key] = {
            "name": obdlib.pid_name(int(key, 16)), "unit": p["unit"], "n": len(times),
            "hz": len(times) / seconds if seconds else 0.0,
            "min": min(vals) if vals else None, "max": max(vals) if vals else None,
            "mean": statistics.fmean(vals) if vals else None,
            "max_gap": max(gaps) if gaps else 0.0,
            "no_data": p["no_data"], "errors": p["errors"],
        }
    return {
        "src": srcs.pop(), "adapter": header.get("adapter"),
        "protocol": header.get("protocol"), "vin_hash": header.get("vin_hash"),
        "seconds": seconds, "samples": len(samples),
        "rate": len(samples) / seconds if seconds else 0.0,
        "gps": sum(1 for r in records if r["type"] == "gps"),
        "ended": footer["reason"] if footer else "no footer (session did not end cleanly)",
        "events": events, "pids": out,
    }


def _f(v, width=8):
    return f"{v:{width}.2f}" if v is not None else " " * (width - 1) + "-"


def render(s, path, torn=False):
    lines = [f"== {path}"]
    if s["src"] != "live":
        lines.append(f"!! {s['src'].upper()} DATA: not from a real car")
    lines += [
        f"src={s['src']}  adapter={s['adapter']}  protocol={s['protocol']}  "
        f"vin_hash={s['vin_hash']}",
        f"{s['seconds']:.1f} s, {s['samples']} samples, {s['rate']:.1f} samples/s, "
        f"{s['gps']} gps fixes, ended: {s['ended']}" + (", torn last line" if torn else ""),
        "",
        f"{'PID':4} {'signal':32} {'n':>6} {'Hz':>6} {'min':>8} {'mean':>8} {'max':>8} "
        f"{'unit':6} {'gap s':>6} {'nodata':>6} {'errors':>6}",
    ]
    for key, p in s["pids"].items():
        lines.append(f"{key:4} {p['name'][:32]:32} {p['n']:6d} {p['hz']:6.2f} "
                     f"{_f(p['min'])} {_f(p['mean'])} {_f(p['max'])} {p['unit']:6} "
                     f"{p['max_gap']:6.2f} {p['no_data']:6d} {p['errors']:6d}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("events: " + (", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(s["events"].items()))
                               or "none"))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("logs", nargs="+")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    for path in args.logs:
        records, torn = obdlog.read_log(path)
        print(render(summarize(records), path, torn))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""obdsum: per-session and per-PID summary of a drive log."""
import os
import unittest

import obdlog
import obdsum

                       "drive-cycle-synth.jsonl")


class Summary(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.records, _ = obdlog.read_log(FIXTURE)
        self.s = obdsum.summarize(self.records)

    def test_session_fields(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.s["src"], "synth")
        self.assertGreater(self.s["seconds"], 15)
        self.assertGreater(self.s["rate"], 5)

    def test_per_pid_counts_add_up(self):
        n = sum(1 for r in self.records if r["type"] == "sample")
        self.assertEqual(sum(p["n"] for p in self.s["pids"].values()), n)
        self.assertEqual(self.s["samples"], n)

    def test_per_pid_stats(self):
        rpm = self.s["pids"]["0C"]
        self.assertLessEqual(rpm["min"], rpm["mean"])
        self.assertLessEqual(rpm["mean"], rpm["max"])
        self.assertGreater(rpm["hz"], 0)
        self.assertGreater(rpm["max_gap"], 0)

    def test_events_are_counted_per_pid(self):
        recs = self.records[:3] + [
            {"type": "event", "src": "synth", "seq": 99, "t_mono": 0, "t_wall": "",
             "event": "no_data", "pid": "0C"}]
        s = obdsum.summarize(recs)
        self.assertEqual(s["events"]["no_data"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(s["pids"]["0C"]["no_data"], 1)

        text = obdsum.render(self.s, FIXTURE)
        self.assertIn("SYNTH", text)

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.310/8a1e2064229c0bbd3b02104a90facdb4/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |
